# estimation.reparam { #wdm.estimation.reparam }

`estimation.reparam`

Constrained/unconstrained parameter transforms.

The filter propagates a Gaussian belief. Metabolic parameters are not Gaussian
quantities: time constants and gains are strictly positive, the adaptation gain
lies in $[0, 1)$, and a Gaussian placed on any of them puts mass on
impossible values. Worse, a sigma point drawn from such a belief can *be* an
impossible value, and a negative time constant does not merely give a poor
estimate -- it makes the dynamics explode.

The fix is to filter in an unconstrained coordinate $\eta$ and map to the
natural parameter only inside the dynamics. Every transform here is centered so
that $\eta = 0$ recovers the prior and scaled so that $\eta \sim
N(0, 1)$ spans a physiologically plausible range. The prior is therefore exactly
the standard normal, and the initial parameter covariance is the identity --
which is not a coincidence but the point of choosing the scales this way.

## Classes

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [ParamTransform](#wdm.estimation.reparam.ParamTransform) | The full set of per-parameter transforms, in `PARAM_NAMES` order. |
| [Transform](#wdm.estimation.reparam.Transform) | One parameter's map from unconstrained ``eta`` to natural units. |

### ParamTransform { #wdm.estimation.reparam.ParamTransform }

```python
estimation.reparam.ParamTransform(rmr_intercept_prior, rmr_slope_prior)
```

The full set of per-parameter transforms, in `PARAM_NAMES` order.

Built from the subject's expenditure prior so that the two metabolic-rate
coefficients are centered on Mifflin-St Jeor scaled by activity level, rather
than on an arbitrary constant.

#### Methods

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [constrain](#wdm.estimation.reparam.ParamTransform.constrain) | Unconstrained vector to natural-unit `Params`. |
| [prior_cov](#wdm.estimation.reparam.ParamTransform.prior_cov) | The prior covariance, the identity by construction. |
| [prior_eta](#wdm.estimation.reparam.ParamTransform.prior_eta) | The prior mean, which is the origin by construction. |
| [unconstrain](#wdm.estimation.reparam.ParamTransform.unconstrain) | Natural-unit `Params` back to the unconstrained vector. |

##### constrain { #wdm.estimation.reparam.ParamTransform.constrain }

```python
estimation.reparam.ParamTransform.constrain(eta)
```

Unconstrained vector to natural-unit `Params`.

##### prior_cov { #wdm.estimation.reparam.ParamTransform.prior_cov }

```python
estimation.reparam.ParamTransform.prior_cov(scale=1.0)
```

The prior covariance, the identity by construction.

``scale`` above 1 widens the prior uniformly, which is the honest thing
to do if you suspect your logging is unusual in some way the literature
priors do not anticipate.

##### prior_eta { #wdm.estimation.reparam.ParamTransform.prior_eta }

```python
estimation.reparam.ParamTransform.prior_eta()
```

The prior mean, which is the origin by construction.

##### unconstrain { #wdm.estimation.reparam.ParamTransform.unconstrain }

```python
estimation.reparam.ParamTransform.unconstrain(p)
```

Natural-unit `Params` back to the unconstrained vector.

### Transform { #wdm.estimation.reparam.Transform }

```python
estimation.reparam.Transform(kind, center, scale)
```

One parameter's map from unconstrained ``eta`` to natural units.

``kind`` is one of:

``"log"``
    ``theta = center * exp(scale * eta)``. Strictly positive; ``scale`` is
    the standard deviation in log units, so 0.25 means roughly +-25 %.
``"logit"``
    ``theta = sigmoid(logit(center) + scale * eta)``. Confined to ``(0, 1)``.
``"affine"``
    ``theta = center + scale * eta``. Unbounded, for parameters whose sign
    is genuinely unknown.
